Infrastructure for continually self‑improving agents 

 
 
 
 

 

English 中文

 

Reef is the first open-source infrastructure for continual self-improving agents.
It connects agent inference, feedback, learning, and versioned delivery. Use it
to train model weights with Slime and SGLang, or improve an agent's harness, including its prompts, rules, and skills.

 

 🚀 Get started 
🗺️ Roadmap 
🗓️ Office Hours 
📣 Launch post 
💬 Join Discord 
📱 Join WeChat Group 

 

 📰 News

- 2026-11: We are refactoring Reef to a control plane + workers architecture. Some recipes and examples can fail on main until the refactor is complete. If a recipe fails, please open an issue.
- 2026-11: A scenario can split its traffic across its served artifacts 1227, also through Semantic Router 859. The new python harness adapter evolves a Python program 1242.
- 2026-10: Tinker runs as a training component 901. Episodes and agents can run in Modal Sandboxes 942. The artifact repository can live on Hugging Face 1003. New recipe: OPD 683.
- 2026-09: reef-infra v0.1.0 is on PyPI. New recipes: GEPA, SDFT, SDPO and Meta-Harness. Reef serves the OpenAI Responses API at /v1/responses 528.
- 2026-08: Reef is open source. Read the launch post.

 🎯 When to use Reef

Use Reef when you want your agent to keep improving simply by learning from how you interact with your agent.

 Your goal Learning path What you need 
 --- --- --- 
 Keep getting stronger model designed for you Model weight training A trainable model, a supported GPU stack, and feedback your recipe can use 
 Get your harness to self-improve Harness optimization A model endpoint, representative tasks, and an evaluator; no local training GPUs 
 Scientific discoveries Test-time training An execution environment, a correctness checker, and a measurable objective 

 🧩 How Reef fits your stack

 Ability Inference engine (vLLM, SGLang, …) RL training framework (Slime, veRL, AReaL, …) Reef 
 --- :---: :---: :---: 
 Serves live traffic ✅ ❌ ✅ 
 Trains weights ❌ ✅ ✅ 
 Version management ❌ ❌ ✅ 
 Stays live through updates ❌ ❌ ✅ 
 Evolves beyond weights (skills, harness) ❌ ❌ ✅ 

 🔄 How it works

 
 
 
 
 
 

Reef processes each learning cycle in four steps. The table also shows which
modules implement each step.

 Step What happens Where it lives 
 --- --- --- 
 1 · Serve Serve agent requests and record interactions. api/ — agent requests and interaction records inference/ — inference and artifact updates 
 2 · Observe Match feedback to recorded interactions. storage/scenario/records.py — stored interactions and feedback samples/ — feedback matching, eligibility, and samples 
 3 · Grow Produce an update from eligible records. recipe/ — recipe integration train/ — the training pipeline, job data, and training jobs 
 4 · Commit Apply the configured selection policy and publish accepted updates. evaluation/ — candidate evaluation artifact/ — version history and snapshot components

 Reef's artifact and checkpoint functionality requires the git-lfs system
 package. Reef initializes Git LFS locally for its artifact repositories.

We recommend uv for managing packages, and the
commands below use it.

Reef supports two learning surfaces: model weights and agent harnesses .
The deployment's recipe determines which surface its scenarios update.

Send inference requests through Reef and report a score for each response. The
SAO recipe uses each eligible scored rollout to run a training step.

Reef's inference endpoint is OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible: /v1/chat/completions ,
 /v1/responses and /v1/messages take the provider's own request body. A request includes the
 x-reef-scenario header. Inference requests do not create scenarios or select recipes. Create
the scenario with POST /reef/scenarios ; it uses the deployment's configured recipe. Then wait
until GET /reef/scenarios/{scenario}/inference/status reports ready .

The response body uses the provider's OpenAI-compatible format. Reef adds the
 x-reef-agent-record-id response header. Its value is the receipt that a
later report uses to identify this interaction. A report can contain a numeric

example reports both a score and a short explanation.

for recipes that read more than a scalar. The endpoint will validate the

 Watch it learn and grow

Once the recipe has enough feedback, Reef submits a training job to the
training component. When a checkpoint that the job saved passes evaluation,
the inference runtime loads it as the new snapshot. Later inference requests
use the current version without restarting Reef.

install.html:
💡 Note

Reef's artifact and checkpoint functionality requires the git-lfs system package. Reef initializes Git LFS locally for its artifact repositories.

We recommend uv for managing packages, and the commands below use it.

From PyPI
uv venv && source .venv/bin/activate
uv pip install reef-infra
python3 -c "import reef; print(reef.__version__)"
From source
git lfs install
git clone https://github.com/Human-Agent-Society/reef.git
cd reef
uv venv && source .venv/bin/activate
uv pip install -e .
python3 -c "import reef; print(reef.__version__)"

Use the source checkout for development and for the training examples below.

usage.title: Using Reef
usage.html:
Reef supports two learning surfaces: model weights and agent harnesses. The deployment's recipe determines which surface its scenarios update.

As a minimal example, start Reef as a pure inference server. This needs SGLang and GPU-enabled PyTorch in the environment:

reef serve --inference.model-path Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct
Weight-training deployment
Start the deployment

The following example starts the SAO (arXiv:2607.07508) example deployment. Run it from a Reef checkout in an environment that satisfies the GPU requirements in Evolve your model.

uv pip install -e ".[slime]" && uv pip install --no-deps --group runtime

export MODEL_PATH="Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct"
export REEF_TOKEN="reef-local"

reef serve -c recipes/sao/examples/imo_answerbench/serve.yaml \
  --inference.model-path "$MODEL_PATH" \
  --reef.port "8900"

curl -f http://127.0.0.1:8900/healthz          # the service is up
Send an inference request and report feedback

Send inference requests through Reef and report a score for each response. The SAO recipe uses each eligible scored rollout to run a training step.

Reef's inference endpoint is OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible: /v1/chat/completions, /v1/responses and /v1/messages take the provider's own request body. A request includes the x-reef-scenario header. Inference requests do not create scenarios or select recipes. Create the scenario with POST /reef/scenarios; it uses the deployment's configured recipe. Then wait until GET /reef/scenarios/{scenario}/inference/status reports ready.

The response body uses the provider's OpenAI-compatible format. Reef adds the x-reef-agent-record-id response header. Its value is the receipt that a later report uses to identify this interaction. A report can contain a numeric score, textual or structured feedback, and the receipts it evaluates. This example reports both a score and a short explanation.

import os
import time

import httpx

scenario = "hello-reef"
reef = httpx.Client(
    base_url="http://127.0.0.1:8900",
    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['REEF_TOKEN']}", "x-reef-scenario": scenario},
    timeout=300,
)

# Create the scenario; a repeated request returns the existing scenario
reef.post("/reef/scenarios", json={"name": scenario}).raise_for_status()

# Wait until inference is ready for the scenario
deadline = time.monotonic() + 1800
while True:
    startup = reef.get(f"/reef/scenarios/{scenario}/inference/status")
    startup.raise_for_status()
    status = startup.json()
    if status["state"] == "ready":
        break
    if status["state"] == "failed":
        raise RuntimeError(f"Inference startup failed: {status['error']}")
    if time.monotonic() > deadline:
        raise TimeoutError(f"Inference is still {status['state']} after 30 minutes; read the Reef logs")
    time.sleep(1)

# Send a provider-compatible inference request
response = reef.post(
    "/v1/chat/completions",
    json={
        "model": os.environ["MODEL_PATH"],
        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Return exactly: reef is ready"}],
    },
)

response.raise_for_status()
receipt = response.headers["x-reef-agent-record-id"]
answer = response.json()["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]

# Sending report about the inference
matched = answer.strip() == "reef is ready"

reef.post(
    "/reef/report",
    json={"score": float(matched), "feedback": "matched" if matched else "wrong answer", "references": [receipt]},
).raise_for_status()

feedback carries the richer signal, plain text or a structured object, for recipes that read more than a scalar. The endpoint will validate the report schema (reef/core/reports/).

Watch it learn and grow

Once the recipe has enough feedback, Reef submits a training job to the training component. When a checkpoint that the job saved passes evaluation, the inference runtime loads it as the new snapshot. Later inference requests use the current version without restarting Reef.

Harness-evolving deployment

Evolve a coding agent's skills and rules from scored feedback, using a model API instead of GPUs.

A harness deployment serves reef.recipe.harness:HarnessEvolutionRecipe. The recipe keeps the agent harness as a tree of text files. At each step, a method edits a copy of that tree from the step's traces, the evaluation runs the real agent on tasks with the candidate, and a candidate that wins publishes as a snapshot that any client can pull. The harness evolution tutorial runs the smallest full loop on pi. It needs an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and Node.js and npm for pi. From your Reef checkout and activated Python environment:

cd tutorials/evolve-your-harness
./run.sh

configs/serve.yaml names the endpoint (inference.upstream-url, no /v1 suffix) and the model (inference.upstream-model). Edit them to point at your own provider, and set REEF_UPSTREAM_API_KEY if the endpoint needs a key. run.sh starts Reef on 127.0.0.1:8900, sends the tasks through it, reports each score, and pulls the published tree. Each run writes work/replay.html with the snapshot chain and the files each step changed.

GET /reef/harness serves the published tree, rendered for the deployment's adapter. The files carry no endpoint, key, or model: a client writes them where the agent reads them and binds the agent's model to this Reef (see Use a published tree). Write the tree outside the project the agent works in: a session can write files in its project, so a tree there could change what the next session runs. Evolve agent prompts, rules, and skills explains the loop and its configuration.
